title: A primitive root gives an etale basis on every scheme over its field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $m\geq1$ be an integer, and let $\zeta\in k$ have multiplicative order exactly $m$ (a primitive $m$-th root of unity). Let $T$ be any $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. On its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $(\mathbf Z/m)_T$ be the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and let $\mu_{m,T}$ be the sheaf of units $z$ with $z^m=1$ [def-asd-etale-roots-of-unity], regarded as a $\mathbf Z/m$-module by powers. The morphism
$$(\mathbf Z/m)_T\longrightarrow\mu_{m,T},\qquad a\longmapsto\zeta^a$$
induced by the constant root section is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathbf Z/m$-modules. No finite-type, reducedness, connectedness or algebraic-closedness hypothesis is imposed on $T$ or $k$.
